title: Matters emerges from stealth with $5M in pre-seed funding to build AI-native consumer bank
summary: AI-powered personal finance startup Matters has emerged from stealth with $5 million in pre-seed funding to develop a consumer banking platform focused on helping users manage their spending and increase their savings. The round was led by Swedish angel investor Jakob Johansson, with participation from Knut Frängsmyr (former COO of Klarna), Douglas Stark (Voi co-founder), Johan Bladh (CEO of Röko), Patrik Tran (CEO of Validio), and Per Widerstrom (CEO of Evoke). Matters was founded by Per Österström with the aim of building an AI-native consumer bank that combines automation and personalised financial guidance to help customers improve their financial wellbeing. The company's planned offering combines neobank services with an AI Advisor designed to help users make more informed spending decisions, increase savings and work towards their financial goals. Customers will pay a flat monthly subscription fee, while revenue streams typically retained by banks, such as interchange revenue and foreign exchange fees, will be returned to users through an accumulated cashback system. Through this model, Matters aims to align its business interests with those of its customers, focusing on customer experience, retention and long-term loyalty. title: From Slush to sustainable materials: Ambio raises €5.1M for AI-powered plastics procurement
summary: Helsinki-based startup Ambio has raised a €5.1 million seed round led by b2venture , with participation from Montis and existing investor Lifeline Ventures , to bring greater trust, reliability, and speed to recycled plastics procurement. Founded in February 2023 by two former Slush team members, Ambio is developing an AI-powered, end-to-end procurement platform that makes recycled plastics easier to source, assess, and trade, covering the entire purchasing cycle from material discovery and sampling to long-term deliveries. I spoke to co-founders CEO Tommi Bergström and CPO Elmo Pakkanen to learn more. Fragmented supply and inconsistent quality hinder plastics recycling According to Bergström, the recycled plastics market remains fundamentally broken. "Supply is highly fragmented, quality is unpredictable, pricing is inefficient, and there isn't a reliable way for materials to be traded and moved." In the European Union alone, roughly 50,000 companies use plastics as raw materials, compared with approximately 1,500 companies recycling them. While plastic might appear to be a straightforward commodity, there are thousands of variations, and manufacturers require specific grades for different applications. Finding the right material among Europe's recyclers can therefore be a significant challenge. Quality presents another obstacle, particularly with post-consumer recycled plastics. title: Solvera raises $6.3M to scale the AI-native engineering firm
summary: Oslo-based Solvera has raised $6.3 million in a pre-seed funding round to develop its AI-native engineering firm for the construction industry. The round was led by Seedcamp , with participation from Construct Venture, Inception Fund, Momentum, Obos Ventures, PSV Tech, Sondo, and The Nordic Web Ventures, alongside angel investors including Spacemaker founders Anders Kvåle and Håvard Haukeland. Founded by Arif Mirza (CEO), Pål Rasmussen (CTO), and Thorvald Thorsnes (CCO), Solvera is building an engineering firm that combines AI technology with the expertise of experienced building engineers. Rather than offering software licences or charging for consulting hours, the company provides end-to-end engineering services, taking projects from initial requirements and constraints through to coordinated, construction-ready designs. At the centre of its approach is a purpose-built operating system that uses AI agents to automate an increasing share of engineering tasks, while human engineers remain responsible for judgement and key decisions. The system is designed to improve with each project by capturing engineering knowledge and making it reusable across future work.
